/rulesets.name: Unconstrained (No Limits)
/rulesets.description: No limits: no daily loss cap, no profit target, no drawdown floor, no contract ladder, no halts. Measures the strategy's raw behaviour — not whether it would pass an account's rules. Pair with manual sizing to make X% mean exactly X%.

/rulesets.name: Personal Forex — 55% Drawdown
/rulesets.description: Forex risk tolerance: fail at 55% drawdown from peak, no other limits. The gradeable counterpart to Unconstrained — same raw behaviour, but with the one bar stated, so a stress test can return a letter instead of 'not graded'.

/rulesets.name: Futures Flex $50k Challenge
/rulesets.notes: One-time fee (base ~$134; promo code FLEX ~$69.99; reset ~$78). No activation fee to funded. DRAWDOWN: EOD trailing $1,500, locks permanently at $50,100 ($100 above start), then stops trailing. NO daily loss limit (MLL only). CONSISTENCY 40% CHALLENGE-PHASE ONLY -- UNUSUAL MECHANIC: breaching it does NOT fail the account; it RAISES the profit target instead. 40% rule mathematically forces >=3 winning days (no separate min-days rule found). CONTRACTS fixed (no scaling), 3 mini / 30 micro, mixable at 1:10; exceeding = excess-contract profit voided (penalty, not breach). Intraday only: flat by 3:10pm CT (16:10 ET, DST-adjusted), no overnight/weekend, auto-closed if left open. News trading allowed. Automated/EA/bots allowed (no latency abuse / order flooding). PROHIBITED: tight-bracket/no-slippage exploitation, grid, hedging, correlated-instrument hedging, trading within 2% of CME price limit. Platforms NinjaTrader + Tradovate. allowed_instruments = standard CME set we trade; verify exact FundedNext product list. Verified from docs_url on 2026-05-31.

/strategies/b_leg.name: B-LEG

param_schema.name: bleg_max_days
param_schema.label: Days to watch for the late retrace
param_schema.desc: How long the order waits for the late pullback before the setup is dropped. Counted in bars, so weekends and the daily close do not use it up.
guide: Waits longer for a late return — 4 to 5 days tested best

param_schema.name: exec_risk_pct
param_schema.label: Risk % per trade
param_schema.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. The stop distance sets the position size, so a tighter stop buys a bigger position at the same risk.

param_schema.name: exec_longs
param_schema.label: Trade longs
param_schema.desc: Lets long setups trade. Off = shorts only.

param_schema.name: exec_shorts
param_schema.label: Trade shorts
param_schema.desc: Lets short setups trade. Off = longs only.

param_schema.name: exec_no_late_day
param_schema.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-17:00 NY)
param_schema.desc: On = no new entries in the last hour before the daily close, so a trade cannot be gapped out over the break.

param_schema.name: exec_runner_trail
param_schema.label: Runner trail method
param_schema.desc: How the stop follows the trade once the second target is hit. Fixed step is a plain dollar grid; structure parks it at the last swing.
guide: Fixed step — simplest, and the worst of the three
Structure + ratchet — best on the main bot, untested here

param_schema.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
param_schema.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
param_schema.desc: How many ticks beyond the last swing the trailing stop sits, so a wick through it does not clip you.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

param_schema.name: exec_trail_pct
param_schema.label: Runner ratchet step (% of price)
param_schema.desc: How big each trailing step is, as a percent of price. Keep it small here - these trades risk very little of the price.
guide: Tighter — banks more of each run on this setup
Too big and the stop never moves at all here

param_schema.name: exec_trail_step
param_schema.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
param_schema.desc: The step size in dollars. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

param_schema.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
param_schema.label: TP2 → stop floor
param_schema.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit. TP1 is tight and can scratch the trade; breakeven gives it the most room.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

param_schema.name: exec_time_stop_mode
param_schema.label: Time stop
param_schema.desc: Closes a trade that has been open longer than the hours set below. Before TP1 only cuts trades that never reached the first target.
guide: Off — the clock never closes a trade
Always — the clock closes winners too

param_schema.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
param_schema.label: Time stop (hours)
param_schema.desc: How long a trade may stay open, in hours, weekends included.
guide: Cuts winners as well as losers

param_schema.name: exec_aplus
param_schema.label: SOS Fade has priority (stand the B-leg down)
param_schema.desc: On = stand down on any side where the main reversal setup would have armed, which keeps results comparable with the parent. Off = every setup trades on its own.

options.on: SOS Fade stands the B leg down

/strategies/b_leg.edge: This is the reversal whose pullback turned up late. Structure breaks, but instead of pulling back the market runs on, so the normal setup dies with no trade at all. This one remembers the level and leaves an order there for a few days in case price comes back. Often it does. Everything after the entry is handled the same way as the main bot.

steps.label: 01 · Break
steps.title: A reversal fires
steps.detail: Structure breaks and the level to watch is marked, even though the reversal itself has not traded yet.

steps.label: 02 · Runs on
steps.title: The pullback never comes
steps.detail: Price expands and breaks structure again before pulling back, so the normal reversal dies with no trade. That death is what starts this setup.

steps.label: 03 · Late
steps.title: The pullback arrives anyway
steps.detail: An order rests at the marked level for a few days. If price comes back to it, the order fills. If it never comes back, or runs too far the other way, the setup is dropped.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Let it run
steps.detail: The same machinery as the main bot: the first target moves the stop to breakeven, the second lifts it further, and the trailing stop takes the rest.
